newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal's 1996/97 GDP growth rate slows.
newsitem.headline: Nepal's 1996/97 GDP growth rate slows.

text.p: Nepal's gross domestic product (GDP) growth slowed in the first nine months of fiscal 1996/97 due to a decline in agricultural production, a Finance Ministry report said on Thursday.
Nepal's fiscal year runs from mid-July to mid-July.

The Economic Survey, an evaluation of the state of the economy, said GDP was estimated to grow by 4.9 percent in the first nine months of 1996/97. It did not give comparative figures for the same period in the previous year.
Nepal's GDP grew by 6.1 percent in 1995/96.
"The decline in the growth rate of GDP...is mainly due to the decline in the growth rate of agricultural and non-agricultural sectors," the survey said.
Agriculture, which contributes nearly half of total GDP, is estimated to grow at 3.3 percent in the first nine months of 1996/97 compared with 5.4 percent in the same period a year ago.
The farm sector provides employment to more than 80 percent of the tiny Himalayan kingdom's 22 million people.
The non-agricultural sector, comprising industry and services, grew by 6.1 percent in the first nine months of 1996/97 against 6.7 percent in the corresponding period a year earlier.
"It would be a challenge to increase investments for production by increasing the rate of gross domestic savings," the survey said.
Nepal's trade deficit widened to 52.08 billion rupees ($917.7 million) in the first nine months, an increase of 29 percent from the corresponding period in the previous year.
Imports grew 25.6 percent to 69.03 billion rupees in the first nine months of 1996/97 while exports rose 16.3 percent to 16.9 billion rupees in the same period.
The balance of payment surplus for the first eight months of 1996/97 stood at 598.5 million rupees, the survey said. It gave no comparative figure for the corresponding period in the previous year.
The report said the services sector had to be developed and foreign investment needed to be wooed to maintain the favourable balance of payment situation.
"During the review period of the current fiscal year, in comparison to the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year, some improvement is seen on current account deficit," the survey said.
"The reason for this is being the increase in the service (net) and transfers (net) amount," it added.
The current account deficit stood at 9.84 billion rupees in the first eight months of 1996/97. The comparative figure for the previous year was not available.
